entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Accused Nos.2 and 3 in S.T. No.446 of 2000 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Idukki filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2(ia)m , 7(i) and 16(1)
(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short 'the PFAAct') read with A. 05.05.01 of PFA Rules.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Idukki
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 18.12.1999 at about 11 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, Kanjikuzhy, purchased six packets of Ammu chilly powder from the shop of the first accused.
First accused was the proprietor and the second accused was the manufacturer.
Third accused was the company represented by the second accused.
After complying with the legal formalities, samples were taken.
Thereafter, one of the sample was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.

The Public Analyst filed Ext. P10 certificate stating that the food item did not conform to the standard prescribed for chilly powder under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P15 were marked for the prosecution.
Exts.D1 to D6 were marked on the side of the revision petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P10 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, Admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext.10 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra)
that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not C.B. Ramesh vs State Of Kerala on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102751148/
2 admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

entities.text: C.B. Ramesh vs State Of Kerala on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision of the Pepsico India Holdings (supra)'s case, the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2(ia)m , 7(i) and 16(1)(a)(i) of the PFA Act read with A. 05.05.01 of PFA Rules and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bonds of the revision petitioners stand cancelled and they are set at liberty.

Sd/-
B.SUDHEENDRA KUMAR, JUDGE dl/.12.1.2016 // True Copy // PA to Judge C.B. Ramesh vs State Of Kerala on 7 January, 2016
